title: Notion vs. OneNote: Which note-taking app should you use? [2026]
summary: We compared Notion vs. OneNote in depth to help you decide which note-taking app makes the most sense for your needs.
body_markdown:
**Notion**


**OneNote**


**Ease of use**


⭐⭐⭐⭐ Easy to start, but there's so much freedom that there can be a learning curve for beginners


⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Follows the traditional notes and notebooks structure, making it very easy to pick up and use


**Notes**


⭐⭐⭐⭐ Structured block layout with multimedia support; no drawing or handwriting


⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Freeform canvas with text, drawings, handwriting, audio, video, and equations


**Security and offline access**


⭐⭐⭐ Individual pages can't be locked with passwords; offline access requires downloading pages ahead of time


⭐⭐⭐⭐ Password-protected notes; desktop app keeps all notebooks on your device and syncs whenever there's a connection


**Collaboration**


⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Shared workspaces with comments, mentions, and real-time editing


⭐⭐⭐ Share notes with others; real-time collaboration, but no comments or mentions


**AI**


⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Notion Agent handles multi-step tasks, searches connected apps, and takes meeting notes; requires the Business plan


⭐⭐⭐ Copilot writes, summarizes, and answers questions from your notes; included with Microsoft 365 Personal and above


**Pricing**


⭐⭐⭐⭐ Generous free plan with no page limit or storage cap for solo users (except a 5 MB file upload limit); paid plans start at $10/user/month, billed annually


⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Free plan includes 5 GB of OneDrive storage; paid plans start at $1.67/month for 100 GB; Copilot AI features start with the $8.33/month Microsoft 365 Personal plan


**Integrations**


⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Connects to thousands of apps with Zapier; native connections to apps like Slack and Google Drive


⭐⭐⭐⭐ Connects to thousands of apps with Zapier; works seamlessly with the rest of Microsoft 365
